newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks buoyed by inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks buoyed by inflation data.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed higher Friday for the first time this week as news that wholesale prices edged up only slightly last month helped the market to overcome worries about upcoming corporate earnings.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 47.71 points to 5,969.38, bouncing back from four consecutive sessions of losses. For the week, the Dow fell 23.48.
The index traded briefly with a gain of 50 points, which activated the New York Stock Exchange's limits on programme trading.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,433 to 864 on moderate volume of 395 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The upturn came on the sixth anniversary of the bull market, which started on Oct. 11, 1990.
The Dow index cracked the 6,000 level briefly on Monday and Tuesday, but finished lower both days.
Wall Street cheered news that the Producer Price Index rose only 0.2 percent in September, slightly less than expected, in a sign that inflation remained tame at the wholesale level.
In another report, retail sales increased 0.7 percent last month, well beyond forecasts, but the report included a downward revision of August sales to a 0.2 percent decline.
"It has been a very powerful market," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"We were hitting on all cyliners and what launched it was the combination of good retail sales and a good wholesale inflation number," he said.

In the inflation-sensitive bond market, the bellwether 30-year Treasury rose half a point, and the yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, fell to 6.85 percent from 6.89 percent on Thursday.
Among the big gainers were technology stocks -- especially semiconductors -- brokerage houses and retailers, while the shares of precious metals companies fell.
Morgan Stanley set a positive tone for computer chip stocks with an upgrade of Intel Corp.
Intel, which is expected to announce its quarterly results on Monday, rose 5-1/2 to 105-3/8.

"It was a real barnburner of a day for the technology sector because with tightness in the labour and capital markets, companies are investing in capacity-enhancing technology, so most economists are now revising upward their forecasts for technology spending," Johnson said.
Texas Instruments Inc. rose 1/4 to 55-3/8, Motorola Inc. gained 1/2 to 48-3/4, Atmel Corp. added 1-1/4 to 31-3/8, Applied Materials was up 3/8 to 29-3/4.
International Business Machines Corp. closed up 2-3/8 at 130-1/8, a new 52-week high.

The Nasdaq's most active issue Cascade Communications Corp. was hammered after reporting quarterly results that exceeded Wall Street expectations, but disappointed nonetheless because of a slimmer-than-hoped-for rise vs. the prior quarterly results.
Cascade fell 15-1/8, a 17.5 percent loss, to close at 71-3/8 after almost 16 million shares changed hands.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 11.30 points to 1,248.27.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was up 6.05 to 700.66. The American Stock Exchange index was up 0.42 to 580.41.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.54 to 372.89. The average share was up 27 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,866.278 up 49.722 or 0.73 percent.
